title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
This incident shows a failure of screen verification in a legitimate mobile trading application. Scammers created an AI-generated fake website that displayed false account balances and investment information to the victim while he used a genuine app. The deception relied on the victim having no way to confirm what he saw on his own screen matched his actual account state, either through independent verification or human review before large transactions.

The attack exploited a common gap in financial application design: the absence of out-of-band confirmation for withdrawals. A system that required the victim to verify large transactions through a separate channel, such as a confirmation code sent to his phone number on file, might have exposed the discrepancy before funds were transferred. It is not established whether the scammers compromised the app itself, gained access to the victim's account credentials, or operated entirely through screen manipulation.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message. A stranger contacted Jerry Dunaway and convinced him to invest through a mobile trading app, gradually building trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw funds. Unknown to Jerry, scammers had created an artificial intelligence-generated fake website that displayed false investment information on his screen. When he attempted a larger withdrawal, the scheme collapsed, and he discovered his entire life savings had vanished.

The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, are now speaking publicly to warn others about the elaborate tactics used by scammers. Gwinnett County police confirmed the mobile app was legitimate but the scammers manipulated what appeared on his screen through the fake site. Investigators say victims in these cases rarely recover their stolen money. The couple's children have started a fundraising campaign to help their parents cover basic living expenses as they work with local authorities to investigate the fraud.
